Corvuria (A59)

Survey region (English ranking table): Wescann / Gerudia.

At a glance: Turn a poor border kingdom into a midnight realm quietly controlled by vampire nobles, running a Court of the Crimson Covenant while rebuilding the blighted Folly.

v2.1 personality coordinates: Expansion 89/100 | Autocracy 94/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 84/100 (100 = Magic, 0 = Artifice; theme intensity 86/100) | Pluralism 18/100.

v2.1 values: Evil (23/100), with a mixed trajectory.

Story: High | Mission tree: Long (72 direct mission definitions) | Mission-tree update: Exact rework date unresolved; local version v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: High | Tedium: Medium | Early pressure: Medium-high | Expansion: High.

A Poor Border Kingdom with Two Layers of Power

In 1444, Corvuria is a kingdom ruled from Arca Corvur, not a country that must first be formed. Davan II síl Vivin is on the throne, and his heir, Camir II, is a powerful mage. The history files also place a Vampire estate, the “National Conspiracy” masquerade law, and bloody noble privileges in the opening setup. Asheniande to the east is a historic rival. From day one, the player must manage the royal house, the vampire nobility, and external enemies. [Local script]

Mission text supplies a much older backstory. After the Dragonwake, Korbarid ancestors occupied the old fortress of Bal Dostan and sheltered the local population; their mysterious “patrons” gradually began treating the inhabitants as livestock. The text says vampires have been connected to these lands since the Aldresian Crusade of 1044. Another passage presents the early human king Lucian as negotiating with Jaher and preserving local autonomy under the Phoenix Empire. These are accounts of the past in the Mod's mission narrative, not future objectives already completed by the player. [Local flavor text]

The offline English history of the Kingdom of Corvuria and the Korbarid entry add a longer rise-and-fall arc. In the Dragonwake, the Korbarids occupied the abandoned Bal Dostan; in 666, Daravan's dark ritual flooded the south and created the region later called Daravan's Folly; in 672, the old Castanorian Empire invaded and ended the Korbarid kingdom. Later conquests by Jaher and Jexis, followed by the return of House síl Vivin, layered into the Corvuria of 1444. The Wiki's founding section is marked unfinished, and some dates lack a full explanation, so this article uses only a historical outline compatible with the local narrative and does not infer an inevitable ending. [Offline Wiki]

This history explains why Corvuria is not merely a “vampire conqueror.” It is poor and peripheral, and its royal house needs powerful protection; the price is that the Night's Nobility has embedded itself in the state. Asheniande's separation, the dispute over Ravenhill, and expeditions south after the Greentide give the dynasty's revival concrete military aims. [Local flavor text] [Official development diary]

Mission Future: From the Grand Masquerade to the Court of the Crimson Covenant

The current A59 tree has 72 direct mission definitions in Corvuria_Missions.txt. Early missions ask you to build up the army and confront Asheniande, while also developing the capital, appeasing estates, and investing in livestock and trade. “Corvurian Husbandry” is an ordinary livestock industry; do not confuse it with the separate narrative metaphor that calls people vampire “livestock.” [Local script]

The central turning point is “The Grand Masquerade.” The Vampire estate must have sufficient loyalty and influence, while the influence of the other major estates must be held down. Completing it grants the Midnight Monarchy reform and sets the country flag for embracing vampires. The Court of Blood then organizes the Night's Nobility into a transnational network that can invite vampires from other countries with a Vampire estate. Later, the monarch may choose the power vampires offer in a blood-contract event. To become an eternal ruler, the monarch must also be both a vampire and a powerful mage. An immortal mage-king is therefore a conditional mission future, not a guarantee at the 1444 start. [Local script]

This route has a significant political cost: once the Grand Masquerade is completed and corvurian_embraced_vampires is set, the decision to form Dostanor (Z07) is no longer available. A59's main route builds a Midnight Kingdom under the original Corvuria Tag; Dostanor is only an alternative formable route if the country has not embraced vampires and meets the requirements. It is not an inevitable successor. [Local script]

Beyond the Night, a Long Recovery

The middle and late missions draw Corvuria into imperial politics, the East Cannorian frontier, and competition for southern fortresses; they can also organize the Dark Legion mercenaries. A parallel storyline restores Daravan's Folly: investigate the curse, rebuild the waterways, resettle people, and eventually “Cure the Folly.” The scripts impose multiyear recovery modifiers and resource requirements along the way, so this is a long governance project rather than an instant reward for occupying the region. Missions also reach into fashion, textiles, steel, and urban development, combining dark politics with material reconstruction. [Local script]

But the darkness is not just atmosphere. The capital mission's narrative treats residents as livestock for vampires. After missions involving Asheniande, the Ashfield Harvest event strips the province of tax, production, and manpower development and inflicts severe devastation, while granting production to other provinces. Late-game artificery text also explicitly allows “less than humane” experiments. In contrast, restoring the Folly has real public benefit. The values assessment is Evil 23/100, mixed trajectory, based on these specific harms and remedies—not on vampire identity, monarchy, or warfare. [Local script] [Local flavor text]

What Kind of Player Is It For?

You must survive a weak opening among powerful neighbors, use diplomacy and military strength to handle Asheniande, then manage the Vampire estate's loyalty, influence, and politics of concealment. Two long projects then mirror one another: compete for fortresses and imperial influence abroad, while restoring the Folly and developing the capital and economy at home. It suits players who enjoy gothic politics, powerful mage rulers, estate management, and long-term regional reconstruction. It is a poor fit if you only want relaxed development or dislike a very dark story about the treatment of subjects. [Local script]

The 2021 official vampire development diary described Corvuria as a major vampire homeland and previewed Asheniande, the Folly, and the Court of the Crimson Covenant. That year's implementation status does not replace the current scripts. Player discussions often praise the mission story, while warning that vampire mechanics, proximity to the Empire, and the Crimson Deluge can add pressure. Those are community impressions without a pinned version, not current numerical findings. [Official development diary] [Community views] Full sources and Wiki limitations are in the evidence record.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Corvuria (A59) — Corvurian Ideas

        tag = A59 #Corvuria

Corvurian Traditions

  • Hostile Attrition: +100% (hostile_attrition; raw value 1.0).

  • global_regiment_cost：-10% (global_regiment_cost; raw value -0.1).

1. The Sapphire Key

The Sapphire Key has long been the badge of authority for the rulers of this land. Originally gifted by Castan I to one of two Foaric chiefs, it enabled them to enter the city of Castonath, the association of which allowed the Raven King to enter Bal Dostan and secure Dostanor during the Dragonwake. Since then, the possession of the Sapphire Key has been a symbol of power, from the Korbarids to Great Cardest to the modern síl Vivin kings. Rulers and dynasties come and go, but the key and the power that its possession grants has endured.

  • Stability cost modifier: -20% (stability_cost_modifier; raw value -0.2).

2. A Legacy of Grim Conflicts

For as long as this land has existed, it has been harsh, grim, and cursed.

Daravan the Malignant created the Folly in 669 to fend off the gnollish Drowned Xhaz, drowning the southern half of old Dostanor to no avail for the gnollish survivors, and worse things now threaten our borders. The pogroms committed by the Cardesti and the Korbarids on each other, the Castanorian reconquest of the land by Castan Ebonfrost, the rise of the infamous Corvurian, Nichmer, plunging the continent into war, and finally the White Pestilence - the people here have been hardened and desensitized by cultural traumas over years, and as such, only truly terrifying things can shake a Corvurian..

  • morale_damage_received：-10% (morale_damage_received; raw value -0.1).

3. The Black Thorns

The Order of the Black Thorns is a chivalric order that traces its ancestry back to the Aldresian Crusade. It was the spear-tip of the crusade into the dark heart of Corvuria, which eventually lanced the pustule that caused the pestilence. For this reason, their leader, Lucian síl Vivin, was granted the title of Protector by Jaher, and though he would ultimately disappear, his family and his order would live on, and the Corvurian kings still count the Grand Master of The Black Thorns amongst their titles. Most modern nobles of Corvuria are either a part of or at least had an ancestor who was part of the Order.

The Order of the Black Thorns is known openly for three things: their steadfast, if unorthodox, devotion to Nerat, their brutal and effective skills in war, and their unquestioning loyalty to the síl Vivin kings. Whenever Corvuria is threatened, whether by horrific monsters, terrible undead, or a simple recalcitrant peasant, the Order responds in the same manner: ‘Obliterate, with extreme prejudice.’ Many villages have been left burned to the ground in the wake of a Black Thorn Tribunal, and as such, peasants are quick to denounce their rebellious fellows to prevent their village from becoming the site of the next tribunal.

  • Discipline: +5% (discipline; raw value 0.05).

  • Harsh treatment cost: -20% (harsh_treatment_cost; raw value -0.2).

4. 'I am the Land!'

  • King Daran V síl Vivin-Arannen, in response to criticisms by mages within his court about the overuse of magic to boost agricultural productivity of the land. The mages in question subsequently vanished.

The power and primacy of kings within Corvuria, be they Corvurian, Korbarid, or otherwise, have always been extremely strong. While many other realms, such as Lorent, Dameria, and Wex, at times need to be cautious of upsetting powerful vassals and always must be cognizant of their rights, in Corvuria, the law is clear: the nobility have no enshrined rights except those granted to them by the Holder of the Sapphire Key, and dissent is treason. This temperament became more and more common outside Corvuria in the period of the Age of Witch-Kings, being adopted and maintained by the Arannese even after their subjugation of Corvuria in the 1600s.

  • Maximum Absolutism: +10 (max_absolutism; raw value 10).

5. The Masquerade

Despite the utter dominance of royal power within Corvuria, it is a truly idiotic monarch who would not provide an avenue for advice to be given, and after all, as Queen Celadora once said, “We may die tomorrow, so we’ll drink today.”

A tradition carried over from the Roilsardi crusaders who became the modern Corvurian nobility, the masquerade is a tradition at the heart of the functioning of the state. It is here that all Corvurians, rich and poor, old or young, can intermingle, indulge, and debase themselves freely without fear. Indeed, this is the only chance commoners have to mingle with the nobility. Hosting a grand masquerade is a great honour, solely held to the few nobles who have the king's ear, and those who host the masquerades refresh themselves from such fine conversation and gain new allies or rekindle old ones. Of course, there are some who pointed out that it's always the same families who hold these masquerades, and it always leads to them accruing more power and influence than before.

'Pointed out' being the operative word.

  • Nobility loyalty equilibrium: +10% (nobles_loyalty_modifier; raw value 0.1).

  • Vampire loyalty equilibrium: +10% (vampires_loyalty_modifier; raw value 0.1).

6. Servile Peasantry

Land and laborers are equally poor here, and the only way we can get any richer is to work them both to the bone. Despite the soil being volcanic in nature, the interplay of such strong historic royal prerogatives, the frequent threat of raids from the Folly by gnolls, and holdovers from the effect of the White Pestilence have forced the population to become rather effective farmers and laborers out of necessity. For if they were not so, they would not be so.

  • Production efficiency: +10% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.1).

7. Corvurian Riverine Revival

…For example, investment in logging, mining, and riverine infrastructure along the Carnvord and Dostanesck rivers. With ample resources provided by our Corvurian lands, ably extracted by peasants, and transported to factories in Arannen, I am confident that our realm will be able to cement itself as a leading industrial power. Industrial costs would be lower if it were possible to build factories within Corvuria itself, but the comparative lack of literacy amongst the simpleton workforce as well as… more esoteric concerns render that politically impractical for the time being..."

  • Magister Ostan of Varlosen, in his essay 'A Survey of our Corvurian Lands', to Ostan IV síl Vivin-Arannen, 1801

  • Development cost: -10% (development_cost; raw value -0.1).
